Potential projects for the EPF inception period and longer term in Ukraine, Georgia and Republic of Moldova
In today

s highly interconnected world, the European Union (EU) as a global actor is inevitably affected by changes taking place around the globe, especially in its neighbourhood. This is particularly relevant in the Eastern Partnership countries. The security environment in EU
s Eastern Neighbourhood is characterized by continuous deterioration and increased destabilization actions by foreign actor that directly affects the European security landscape. Partner countries

territories are partly occupied, unresolved and protracted conflicts pose a major security risk, including a high risk of escalation, also continue to hamper political and economic development of those countries. Furthermore, the frozen conflicts limit partner countries

abilities to implement needed reforms and undermine their aspirations to participate in European and Euro-Atlantic structures, where appropriate. Apart from conventional security challenges, multiple risks including corruption, organized crime, cyber and hybrid threats confront the countries in the region, undermining their resilience and stability, as well as their prospects for peace and stability.
In the last Council Conclusions on Eastern Partnership

the EU stressed that strengthening resilience as an overriding policy framework will be one of the key goals for the Eastern Partnership region during the next years. Also, EU has remained firmly committed to its policy of supporting countries

territorial integrity within their internationally recognized borders. Thereby, the European Peace Facility (EPF) assistance measures give the practical means to directly strengthen the ability of partner countries to prevent and respond to crises by bolstering their defence capacities, as well as increase their resilience.

Currently, the EU is contributing to the Eastern Partnership countries via three Civilian Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP) missions, while there are no military CSDP operation deployed in the region. Some Eastern Partnership countries, namely Georgia, Ukraine and Republic of Moldova have contributed to the EU CSDP, proving that cooperation is beneficial for the EU as well. Taking into account the aforementioned fickle security context and The Council Conclusions1 acknowledging the importance of the cooperation in the area of CSDP and the Eastern partners' valuable contribution to EU missions and operations, the EU should prioritize providing assistance to those Eastern Partnership countries, which have contributed to the CSDP. The Joint Communication on
Reinforcing Resilience
an Eastern Partnership that delivers for all

states that the EU will consider providing training opportunities and capacity building to the partner countries, including on countering hybrid threats, where appropriate. These political goals can be realised through building partners
capacities related to the military or defence matters, including the provision of military equipment.
In this context, the EPF offers the EU a very needed and a timely tool. As stated in the Council Decision establishing the EPF
, the EPF aims at strengthening the ability of partner countries to prevent and respond to crises, and contribute to their resilience, in order to enable them to protect their populations better.
On this basis, the support to Ukraine, Georgia and Republic of Moldova fully corresponds to the overall aims of the EPF and it corresponds to the Union

s policy towards these states. Therefore, we, the co-signing Member States of this non-paper, propose this open-ended list of potential projects as the starting point for the EEAS to compose the full range of proposals to be considered for implementation in Ukraine, Georgia and Republic of Moldova as part of the EPF support to their capacities related to the military and defence matters. The proposed projects would directly contribute to their security and stability, including building resilience. Taking into account geographic location of these states in the EU
s immediate neighbourhood, the implementation of these projects would strengthen the EU

s own security. In this regard, the co-signing Member states invite the EEAS to include the project proposals in the draft programme of the upcoming EPF assistance measures and initiate discussions on these matters with Ukraine, Georgia and Republic of Moldova to demonstrate the EU
s intentions to take care of 360-degree security of its immediate neighbourhood.
National Defence Policy of Ukraine, Georgia and Republic of Moldova
Ukraine
After 2014 Ukraine accelerated its defence reforms, which aim at developing Western-type Armed Forces. Currently, Ukraine faces two-folded task

to continue defence reforms and transformation of its Armed Forces, including to increase cooperation with the EU and participation in its military missions and operations, and to strengthen capacities to counter conventional and new types of threats to its sovereignty and territorial integrity.
In 2020, the National Security Strategy of Ukraine was adopted. The Strategy reads Euro-Atlantic integration as a key priority of Ukraine

s national interests and security. Ukraine continues its strategic course, enshrined in the Constitution of Ukraine, on a full-fledged membership in the EU and NATO. The new Strategy focuses on the implementation of national security priorities set out therein, as well as reforms envisioned in the Ukraine-EU Association Agreement and the Ukraine-2020 Sustainable Development Strategy before 2020. Military Strategy of Ukraine (2016) is a combination of fundamental principles and guidelines on security of individual, nation and state. It determines the national policy of Ukraine in the field of defence. Currently, a new draft being proposed which aims for comprehensive reform of the Security Sector, etc. It is planned that the document will be endorsed this year. Strategic Defence Bulletin (SDB) (2016) is a roadmap for Defence Reform. Currently, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) drafts a new SDB which serves as a basis for: 1) State Program of Development of the Armed Forces of Ukraine and other components of Defenc
Georgia

The objective of the MoD of Georgia is to develop Georgian Defence Forces (GDF), their capabilities and to ensure their continuous combat and mobilization readiness and deployability. The military objectives of the GDF are as follows: 1) to ensure deterrence and defence; 2) to contribute into strengthening regional and international security; 3) to provide support to civil authorities during crises, including natural and manmade disasters. In order to plan, coordinate and integrate defence management activities within the MoD, several documents are elaborated or updated regularly
(i) Ministry of Defence Vision 2030
is a Ministry
s long-term visionary document that aims to facilitate the creation of a more agile, sustainable and NATO interoperable Defence Forces; (ii) Strategic Defence Review (SDR)
is a guideline document in line with the MoD Vision 2030 that identifies main directions for the development of the MoD and GDF in 5 year cycle. It aims to develop GDF
s incremental capabilities to create more reliable, task oriented and capable Defence Forces and to enhance GDF interoperability with NATO; (iii) Minister
s Vision Document

provides short-term planning guidance for the Ministry. The document aims to accomplish identified priorities annually in support of overall transformation process and priority development directions outlined in the SDR.
Republic of Moldova

The election of the pro-European President Maia Sandu granted renewed legitimacy to the Republic of Moldova`s European agenda and offers new avenues for cooperation. The reform priorities of the new President are aligned with the EU-the Republic of Moldova Association Agreement and in keeping with the long-term priority objectives of the Eastern Partnership beyond 2020, as spelled out in the Joint Communication by the HR/VP and the Commission on EaP Policy of 18 March 2020

. The main strategic objectives of the Republic of Moldova remain further political association and economic integration with the EU, as well as strengthening political dialogue and relationship with the Euro-Atlantic structures
. The EU

s reaction to this window of opportunity and the level of engagement will be a test for its neighbourhood policies. According to the Law on National Defence, the national defence planning process was institutionalized by outlining procedures and mechanisms to be taken by responsible authorities in drafting strategic documents, including: National Security Strategy, National Defence Strategy (dated 19.07.2018) and Military Strategy (dated 03.10.2018), Strategic Defence Review and Defence Planning Directive of the Ministry of Defence. The National Defence Strategy (approved by the Parliament in July 2018) refers to the EU Global Strategy as an important strategic document, which opens up new opportunities for cooperation between the EU and partner countries. In this context, the Republic of Moldova sets out as one of its main priorities to continue the political dialogue and practical cooperation with the European Union, by intensifying the collaboration in the fields of the common security and defence policy,

s commitment to support the peaceful settlement of the Transnistrian conflict is particularly highlighted. Other programmatic and conceptual documents (Military Reform Concept, Military Doctrine), date back to 2002 and 1995 respectively and will require extensive updates, which are expected to reflect an increased focus on cooperation and interaction with EU CSDP.
Cooperation in the area of CSDP
EU-Ukraine cooperation in the area of CSDP

Ukraine remains one of the most active partners of the EU, including in military-political area. Increasingly close relationship between the EU and Ukraine is reflected in political co-operation: Ukraine is a priority partner within the
HYPERLINK "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Partnership" \o "Eastern Partnership"
Eastern Partnership
and the
HYPERLINK "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Neighbourhood_Policy" \o "European Neighbourhood Policy"
European Neighbourhood Policy

(ENP). Military-political dialogue between the leadership of the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine or the Armed Forces of Ukraine and representatives of the EU institutions (agencies), the EU Military Committee and the EU Military Staff take place on regular basis. Ukraine is being actively engaged in the cooperation with EDA and formalized these relations by signing the Administrative Arrangement in 2015. Within the framework of the military cooperation development, the Work Plan for Cooperation between the Armed Forces of Ukraine and the Secretariat of the Council of the EU (in the field of CSDP) to be signed annually. One of the key priorities of the EU-UA relationship

continue strengthening practical cooperation with the EU in the framework of the Common Security and Defense Policy (involvement of the Armed Forces of Ukraine in the EU-led international peacekeeping operations and the EU Battle Groups).

Ukraine is working on its legal regulation to be able to deploy its national personnel to the EU-led military operation in Bosnia and Herzegovina "EUFOR ALTHEA". In the first half of 2020 Ukrainian designated forces and resources have been involved on standby as a part of the EU Battle Group HELBROC. During the first semester of 2023 the Armed Forces of Ukraine plan to contribute the national pool of forces at the same composition as it was in 2020-1 (Marine Company, Military-transport aircraft IL-76MD with crew and Group of Staff Officers). Furthermore, on request of the EUMS, Ukraine took a decision to contribute to EUBG HELBROC for 2026-1 standby period.
EU-Georgia cooperation in the area of CSDP

Georgia and EU have always shared a productive dialogue in the Eastern Partnership initiative and Georgia has proven to be a reliable partner to the EU including in the area of CSDP. Georgia has been participating in the CSDP military missions and operations for several years and at present provides valuable contributions to the EUTM RCA and EUTM Mali (altogether second largest third state participation).

Georgia reaffirms its commitment to close cooperation with the EU within the CSDP framework in the national strategic documents. The Strategic Defence Review includes a clear intention to continue its active participation in international missions led by the EU (EUTM RCA, EUTM MALI), as well as the bilateral and multilateral cooperation with the EU within the framework of CSDP.
EU-Republic of Moldova cooperation in the area of CSDP

The basis for EU-Republic of Moldova cooperation is the implementation of the Association Agreement, signed in 2014, which also states that parties shall intensify their cooperation in the area of CFSP, including CSDP, and shall address inter-alia the issues of conflict prevention, crisis management and regional stability. A framework for the participation (FPA) of the Republic of Moldova in EU crisis management operations has also been established in 2012. After concluding the FPA, the cooperation between the EU and the Republic of Moldova has deepened with the agreement on security procedures for the exchange and protection of classified information. Participation in CSDP missions and operations is seen by MD authorities as an important dimension of the wider national efforts to promote the Republic of Moldova as a contributor to the international peace and stability. The Republic of Moldova has been making a modest, yet important expert contribution to the European Training Mission in Mali (EUTM Mali) sinc
Taking into account the commitments, that Ukraine, Georgia and the Republic of Moldova have taken towards Euro Atlantic cooperation, as well as the Council
s appreciation of enhanced security dialogue and cooperation with the Eastern partners

, the EU should provide substantial support to capacity building in military and defence areas. The EPF can create an opportunity to strengthen the EU cooperation with Ukraine, Georgia and the Republic of Moldova in the framework in CSDP and to facilitate substantial progress in concrete lines of effort in military-political area.
List of potential areas and examples of projects under the EPF

The list of identified areas in the countries below is submitted in a non-priority order and is non-exhaustive. It reflects the aim of Ukraine, Georgia and the Republic of Moldova to strengthen their ability to prevent and respond to crisis, to contribute to its resilience and to improve their niche/specialized capabilities, which can be deployed in EU operations and missions. Such areas as cyber, CBRN and military medical need to be developed in all three partner countries, therefore, due these similar needs, putting together an assistance measures package which could cover the needs for all three countries should be evaluated as a potential option.

It should be emphasised that the proposed assistance measures are fully in line with the national strategic level documents, as well as the scope and aims of the EPF. We underline the need to engage with other relevant active partners in these three countries, notably NATO and its member states, in order to seek synergies and de-conflict actions.
The areas of potential assistance measures in Ukraine include:
English language training for the Armed Forces;
Upgrade of Armed Forces
training facilities;

Support to Tactical Airlift (An26 ir Mi8) capability deployed in international operations;
Maritime Capability development to counter pirates activities;
Engineer Support Capability; priority
military forces deployed in international operations;
Military units of the Armed Forces, which, potentially, will participate in the EUBGs;
Strengthening cyber capabilities of the Armed Forces and building capacity of cyber experts, establishing training bases/platforms;

Strengthening resilience by building PSYOPS capabilities of the Armed Forces with non-kinetic means (equipment).
The more detailed definitions of proposed assistance measures is in the ANNEX A of this food-for-thought paper.
The areas of potential assistance measures in Georgia include:
Enhancing training and education:
Simulation means (anti-grenade launcher simulators, mortar simulators, remotely controlled heavy target kits, simulator of a short-range portable anti-aircraft missile system);
Development of Georgian Defence Forces Training centres (for Airborne School of the Special Forces Training Centre, and the Sniper School);
Improvement of education and training facilities in the National Defence Academy of Georgia;
Various courses, including in the ESDC, on information security, digitalization, IT protection of critical infrastructure.
Strengthening/Developing Military Medical capability within the Armed Forces;
Strengthening cyber capabilities of the Armed Forces and building capacity of cyber experts:
The Cyber Security Operations Centre (SOC) at the MOD;
Training in cyber security field and the establishment of Cyber class;
Virtual Desktop Infrastructure;
Developing CBRN defence capabilities for deployments in international operations;
Developing Military Police capabilities, both for internal security and for deployments in international operations;
Developing SOF capabilities for deployments in international operations (trainings, courses, equipment provision);
Anti-unmanned aircraft system technology purchase.
The more detailed definitions of proposed assistance measures is in the ANNEX B of this food-for-thought paper.
The areas of potential assistance measures in the Republic of Moldova include:
Strengthening cyber capabilities of the Armed Forces and building capacity of cyber experts;
Strengthening measures countering hybrid threats;
Development of CBRN capabilities of all military units of the Armed Forces;
Development of Military Medical capacity;
Development of EOD capabilities;
Creation of the Simulation Centre of the Armed Forces of Moldova.
The more detailed definitions of proposed assistance measures is in the ANNEX C of this food-for-thought paper.
ANNEX A. UKRAINE
This is a list of examples of concrete projects
proposals for 2021-2022 and longer term
The project proposals require further consultations with Ukraine in terms of the scope of funding, timeframe of implementation respectfully.
1. Developing C-IED (Counter Improvised Explosive Devices) capability
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal
to support developing C-IED capacity of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, deployed abroad and in Ukraine. Outcome
a number of military units of the Armed Forces of Ukraine capable of performing demining activities in accordance with international safety standards.

Background and Rationale. Ukraine is one of the most severely mine affected places in the world, with the most recorded anti-vehicle mine incidents for three years in a row (from 2016) and third globally for overall casualties, behind only Afghanistan and Syria.

C-IED work is primarily the responsibility of the Armed Forces. Since the beginning of the recent conflict in Ukraine, greater focus has been applied on improving C-IED skills among the Armed Forces. Further support for purchasing demining equipment is vital. In addition, Ukraine actively provides contributions to international military operations.

Activities for the project implementation. (1) Equipping units of the Armed Forces of Ukraine with demining equipment deployed in humanitarian demining activities abroad and in Ukraine. Bidding process will be carried out by the MoD of Ukraine. (2) Training of the personnel will be organised by the companies providing equipment. Additional training can be provided on bilateral basis by EU member states.
Resources needed. Further assessment required.
2. Upgrade and modernisation of Combat Training Centre/Airborne Forces Training Centre
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal
to enhance capabilities of Ukrainian Armed Forces 37th Combat Training Centre/199th Airborne Forces Training Centre in Zhytomir. Outcome
well-developed manoeuvre training centre, capable of conducting realistic and demanding joint specialized trainings.
Background and Rationale. Upgrade of Ukrainian military training infrastructure to internationally recognised standards will increase Ukrainian Armed Forces
readiness to counter continued Russian armed aggression against Ukraine
s territory and repeated ceasefire violations by Russia-backed separatists. It will also contribute to improvement of their interoperability with EU and NATO forces, and thus will facilitate Ukraine
s participation in international crisis management operations, including CSDP military missions and operations.
Activities for the project implementation. (1) Reconstruction and modernisation of firing ranges for all types of equipment (tanks, armoured vehicles, artillery

direct and indirect, infantry). (2) Upgrade of Simulation Centre to hold trainings for commands up to brigade level (3) Acquisition of Multifunctional Integrated Laser System for simulations of combat operations up to brigade level and establishment of MILES training facility; (4) Construction of underwater training facility
initially for tank crews
evacuation trainings; (5) training and mentoring for 199th Airborne Forces Training Centre
s personnel.
Resources needed. Initial estimations say about 500 000 euros. Further assessment required.
3. Developing Military Medical capacity
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal
to improve Military Medical capacity of one military medical unit (at Brigade size level). Outcome

fully operational military medical unit able to provide necessary spectrum of services (surgical interventions, including damage control surgery and surgical procedures for emergency surgical cases, deliver life, limb and function saving medical treatment, perform reception/triage of casualties).
Background and Rationale. The MoD of Ukraine is focused on developing new medical structure, improving deployable medical capabilities. This is a pilot project for developing one medical unit.

Activities for the project implementation. (1) Rehabilitation of facilities for the military medical unit. Bidding process will be carried out by the MoD of Ukraine. (2) Equipping the military medical unit. Bidding process will be carried out by the MoD of Ukraine. (3) Training of the personnel will be organised by the companies providing equipment. Additional training can be provided on bilateral basis by EU member states.
Resources needed. Further assessment required
4. Developing operating capabilities of the Joint Centre of Information Assurance and Cyber Defence (JC) of the MoD/Armed Forces of Ukraine [and regional cyber defence centres.]
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal
to develop capacity of the JC of the Armed Forces of Ukraine to carry out its mandate. Outcome
operational JC [and regional cyber defence centres] able to carry out all tasks envisaged in its mandate.

Background and Rationale. Cyber security and defence is one of the priority action areas of the EU and Ukraine. Ukraine faces constant threat of cyber-attacks to its communication and defence systems, including to its national electronic information resources. According to the Cyber security strategy of Ukraine, which was approved by the President of Ukraine on 15th of March 2016, the objective is to create conditions for the safe functioning of cyberspace, application of cyberspace to benefit of individuals, society and the State. It is emphasized that to achieve this goal it is necessary to establish a national cyber security system; enhance the capacity of entities of security and defence sector to the effective fight against military cyber threats, cyber espionage, cyber-terrorism and cyber crime, and also deepen international cooperation in this area; ensure cyber protection of national electronic information resources, and also ensure cyber protection of information infrastructure that is under jurisdic
capabilities will have direct effect on Ukraine
s ability to counter cyber related threats.

Activities for the project implementation. (1) Rehabilitation of facilities of the JC of the Armed Forces [and regional cyber defence centres]. Bidding process will be carried out by the MOD of Ukraine. (2) Equipping the JC [and regional cyber defence centres]. Bidding process will be carried out by the MOD of Ukraine. (3) Personnel training will be organised by the companies
providing equipment. Additional training can be provided on bilateral basis by EU member states.
Resources needed. Further assessment required.
5. Improving CBRN protection capabilities of military units of the regular Armed Forces of Ukraine
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal
to improve personnel protection and detection capabilities of the regular units of the Armed Forces of Ukraine. Outcome
units capable of protecting and detecting CBRN risks in combat/mission environments.
Background and Rationale. CBRN threats remain one of the pertinent risk for troops, including military units deployed in international operations. Currently, Ukrainian Armed Forces

CBRN protection capabilities are ineffective and limited. Improving individual protection and detection measures will allow Armed Forces to operate efficiently in CBRN threat/hazard environment and to minimise negative consequences to military personnel and civilians.

Activities for the project implementation. (1) Equipping military units of the Armed Forces with first-aid self-treatment equipment, individual respiratory protection and protective clothing, personal chemical detection equipment and an individual dosimeter and provision for chemical decontamination of the skin, clothing and individual equipment. Bidding process will be carried out by the MOD of Ukraine. (2) Training of the personnel will be organised by the companies providing equipment. Additional training can be provided on bilateral basis by EU member states.
Resources needed. Further assessment required.
6. Capacity building for Special Operations Forces
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal
to provide a comprehensive
train and equip
assistance to Ukrainian SOF elements to improve their interoperability with NATO (and the EU) counterparts. Outcome
Ukrainian SOF elements fully capable of action in multinational (mainly NATO) settings.
Background and Rationale. Selected elements of Ukrainian SOF are being prepared to be interoperable with NATO (and the EU) Member States
SOF. Success of this endeavour requires further support in equipment, training and training infrastructure upgrade.
Activities for the project implementation. (1) Troops
training, specialist training and courses. (2) Provision of military equipment. (3) Upgrade and modernisation of 142th SOF Training Centre in Berdichev.
Resources needed. Further assessment required.
7. Enhancing Special Operations Forces Informational-Psychological Operations capabilities with non-kinetic equipment (IPSO)
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal
to equip Ukrainian IPSO teams with modern non-kinetic equipment. Outcome
Ukrainian IPSO teams will be equipped to more efficiently conduct counter propaganda operations and psychological protection of the local population in the conflict areas.

Background and Rationale. Ukrainian population faces constant informational and psychological attacks, especially in the conflict regions. After three years of Estonian-Ukrainian cooperation in Psychological Operations workshops, a need to improve Ukrainian IPSO teams

equipment has become apparent in order for them to minimize threats and defend the Ukrainian population from manipulation more efficiently. Better equipment for collecting, analysing information and then producing and disseminating developed products is needed. The faster a team is able to counter malicious narratives on the ground, the higher the probability of success. The equipment needed includes portable work stations with necessary production software, reliable camera and drone equipment, but also GPS devices, generators, radio broadcasting stations and printers.

Activities for the project implementation. (1) Equipping units of the Ukrainian Informational-Psychological Operations with information collecting, analysing, producing and disseminating equipment deployed (or training to be deployed) in conflict area. The equipping process will be based on the ongoing bilateral PSYOPS cooperation between Estonia and Ukraine. (2) Personnel training will be organised by the companies
providing equipment. Additional training will be provided on bilateral basis by EE.
Resources needed (equipment / quantity): GPS (handheld) 10, Laptop computer 18, Production software 18, Photocamera set 10, Mountable camera set 10, Diesel gener

2. Military medical equipment for Army field hospital (Set for 60-Patients).
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal

to improve Military Medical capability within the Armed Forces of Georgia by providing medical equipment for major military medical facilities and specialised units of the Armed Forces in order to provide basic medical services and conduct limited surgery operations, odontology services, etc. for military. Outcome
improved Military Medical services for the Armed Forces.

Background and Rationale. Structure of Military Medicine of the Armed Forces of Georgia: Medical Department of Gen. Staff (a separate branch); Med COY at Each Brigade of the East & West Command (most of them are unmanned); each Battalion structurally has a Med Platoon (unmanned); Military hospital of the MOD in Gori town; Medical Centre in Kutaisi town; Military Maro Makashvili Tserovani Rehabilitation Centre. Major military medical facilities and specialised units of the Armed Forces lack relevant medical equipment for carrying out envisaged medical services.

Activities for the project implementation. (1) Provide medical equipment for major military medical facilities and specialised units of the Armed Forces. Bidding process will be carried out by the MOD of Georgia. (2) Training of the personnel will be organised by the companies providing equipment. Additional training can be provided on bilateral basis by EU member states.
Resources needed. Further assessment required. Initial estimation of costs
3. Cyber security
(1) Equipping the Cyber Security Operations Centre (SOC) at the MoD
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal
to establish and develop SOC
s full operational capability and to provide necessary equipment and training for the personnel. Outcome
strengthened cyber defence capability and improved coordination of activities within the defence sector on countering cyber threats/incidents and protecting critical IT processes.
Background and Rationale. Cyber security is one of the priority action areas of the EU and Georgia. In the Defence Minister
s Vision 2020, cyber resilience is identified as priority area. The MoD is responsible for developing cyber security capabilities at national level.

New centre would strengthen operational performance of the Cyber Security Bureau (CSB) to identify and respond to security incidents, enhance information system security and auditing, and develop related security standards. It is also planned to establish the Cyber Security Laboratory
within SOC, which would allow to detect and to organise cyber defence activities in protecting Government
s websites, other installation to protect from cyber-attacks. SOC will share all necessary standards (NIST, ISO, TOP 20) and will cover all critical processes inside the IT infrastructure.

Main reference documents: the Annual National Program (ANP), the Association Agenda between the EU and Georgia 2017-2020, the Georgian National Cyber Security Strategy and Action Plan 2020-2022 (draft).
Resources needed. Further assessment required.
(2) Training in cyber security field and the establishment of Cyber class in the Defence Institution Capacity-Building School
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal
(1) to provide qualified training in cyber security for the personnel of the National Defence System; (2) to establish specialized Cyber class with computers. Outcome
trained and skilled personnel capable to perform envisaged tasks in cyber security.

Background and Rationale. The MoD recognizes the need to ensure continuous education and training of its cyber security experts, therefore Cyber Security Bureau (CSB) in close coordination with the Defence Institution Capacity-Building School is planning to establish a program for cyber and IT specialists. Equipped Cyber class is needed to conduct specialised technical trainings.

Activities for the project implementation. (1) Funding for the training. (2) Establishing and equipping cyber class in the Defence Institution Capacity-Building School with equipment (computers, etc.).
Resources needed. Further assessment required. Initial estimation of costs
(3) Virtual Desktop Infrastructure

Activities for the project implementation. Arrange VDI in the secret network of MOD, in order to ensure secure, reliable and continuous access to the services from any location in the country for 1000 users.
Resources needed. Further assessment required. Initial estimation of costs

4. Developing CBRN defence capabilities for deployments in international operations (including deployed in international operations, and a light infantry battalion with CBRN Communication and Information Systems (CIS) capability).
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal
to enhance operational CBRN capability of all units of the Armed Forces, including deployed in international operations, and CBRN CIS capability of one infantry battalion. Outcome
enhanced CBRN and CBRN CIS capability of the Armed Forces of Georgia.

Background and Rationale. Countering CBRN risks remains one of the functional area of the Armed Forces. Support to developing CBRN capability will result in avoiding significant reduction in the operational capability of forces operating in a CBRN threat/hazard environment. Also, CBRN capability will allow minimising casualties.
Georgia is active player in this field. Within EU formats, Georgia is engaged in managing CBRN risks

participates in the EU CBRN Risks Mitigation Centre of Excellence (CoE) Initiative and the Centre in Tbilisi operates as one of the eight regional secretariats, which covers Georgia and other South and Eastern European countries. Georgia prepared and approved National Action Plan on CBRN issues in 2015 and was the first CoE partner country to have officially adopted a National Action Plan to counter the risks posed by CBRN materials.

Activities for the project implementation. (1) Equipping units of the Armed Forces with individual and collective counter-CBRN equipment (first-aid self-treatment equipment, individual respiratory protection and protective clothing, personal chemical detection equipment and an individual dosimeter and provision for chemical decontamination of the skin, clothing and individual equipment). Bidding process will be carried out by the MOD of Georgia. (2) Training of the personnel will be organised by the companies providing equipment. Additional training can be provided on bilateral basis by EU member states.
Resources needed. Further assessment required.
5. Developing Military Police capabilities both for internal security and for deployments in international operations:

Activities for the project implementation. (1) Provision of non-lethal equipment (clothing, personal non-offensive equipment, radio systems, vehicles). (2) Construction and provision of equipment for training facility in Tbilisi. (3) Construction and provision of equipment (office equipment, furniture for sleeping rooms and offices) of accommodation and offices in Tbilisi, Gori and Batumi.
Resources needed. Further assessment required.
ANNEX C. REPUBLIC OF MOLDOVA
This is a list of examples of concrete projects
proposals for 2021-2022 and longer term
The project proposals require further consultations with the Republic of Moldova in terms of the scope of funding, timeframe of implementation.
1. Developing CBRN capabilities of all military units of the Armed Forces
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal

to develop CBRN capabilities of all identified military units of the Armed Forces by providing necessary CBRN equipment for treatment capacity, individual protective equipment and detection equipment. Outcome

capable units able to act in hazard environment, able to detect CBRN threats and to treat troops affected by CBRN materials. An immediate objective could be to support the MD Armed Forces to set-up a unit, with the required capabilities, responsible for the mapping and disposal of chemical agents, which still can be found in MDAF inventories and are banned by several international conventions.

Background and Rationale. (i) CBRN threats remain one of the pertinent risk for troops, including deployed in international operations. All three motorized infantry brigades of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Moldova have CBRN subunits (one brigade
CBRN Company, two Brigades
CBRN platoon) which require: 1) capacity: decontamination, disinfection, deactivation; 2) collective equipment: filtration system for unit

s CP, 1xdisinfection tent, 1xdecontamination booth per each subunit, solution for decontamination of personal equipment and weapons; 3) individual protective equipment: gas mask and protective suit for each soldier; 4) detection equipment: individual dosimeters for each soldier, chemical alert device VPHR, radiation detector DP 64. (ii) Provision of the CBRN equipment for personnel deployed in international missions and operations is priority for the Armed Forces. (iii) Support to developing CBRN capability will result in avoiding significant reduction in the operational capability of forces operating in a CBRN threat/hazard environment. Secondly, improved CBRN capability (with early warning system) potentially will allow minimising casualties. (iv) National reference documents: the Long Term Military Capability Development Plan 2020-2030.

Activities for the project implementation. (1) Equipping all units with first-aid self-treatment equipment, individual respiratory protection and protective clothing, personal chemical detection equipment and an individual dosimeter and provision for chemical decontamination of the skin, clothing and individual equipment. Bidding process will be carried out by the MOD of Moldova. (2) Training of the personnel will be organised by the companies providing equipment. Additional training can be provided on bilateral basis by EU member states.
Resources needed. Further assessment required.
2. Developing Military Medical capacity
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal
to equip Military medical service with necessary modern equipment in order to provide all activities envisaged in its mandate. Outcome
fully operational Military medical service that possesses necessary medical equipment, including medical units at brigade level.
Background and Rationale. National reference documents: Law 411/1995 on Health Care, National Defence Strategy and the Action Plan and the Military Strategy and the Action Plan.

Military Medical capacity is critical service for military units, currently being perceived as a critical gap in MDAF. Two medical departments integrated into civilian hospitals (in Chisinau and Balti) provide medical service to the Armed Forces. At brigade level, medical service is provided by the medical units. There is a need to equip the units and train the military medical personnel. On short term the telemedicine capabilities could be one option to overcome the current deficiencies at brigade level by providing focused interventions through remote assistance for emergencies, basic or minor health problems. The modular nature of this capability makes it rapidly implementable. Training could be provided by MS.

Activities for the project implementation. (1) Equipping the Military Medical service and all medical units at brigade level. Bidding process will be carried out by the MOD of Moldova. (2) Training of the personnel will be organised by the companies providing equipment. Additional training can be provided on bilateral basis by EU member states. (3) Additional training Tactical Combat Casualties Care Courses for lifesaver and combat medics.
Resources needed. Further assessment required.
3. Developing EOD (Explosive Ordinance Disposal) capabilities
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal
equipping (tools, techniques, and procedures) and training specialized units of the Armed Forces of Moldova with EOD capabilities. Outcome
equipped and operational specialized units of the Armed Forces of Moldova with EOD capabilities.

Background and Rationale. Current EOD functions include combat engineer reconnaissance (EOR missions); UXO disposal operations (EOD response missions); mine/munitions stocks disposal; surplus (mine/munitions) reduction; demolition works; explosive/munitions demolition; render safe procedures training; mine/UXO awareness training. Moldova also deploys EOD capabilities to international operations.

Activities for the project implementation. (1) Equipping all units of the Armed Forces of Moldova with standard equipment. (2) Training of the personnel will be organised by the companies providing equipment. Additional training can be provided on bilateral basis by EU member states.
Resources needed. Further assessment required.
4. Creating the Simulation Centre of the Armed Forces of Moldova.
Project Goal and Envisioned Outcomes. Goal
develop the Simulation Centre and its curriculum within the Armed Forces of the Republic of Moldova in order to support Specialist training, Armed Forces
CPX exercises, REGEX Exercise and other international exercises, preparation of the Armed Forces contingents for international deployment training. Outcome
capacity to prepare military personnel for conducting military tasks, including for international missions.
Background and Rationale. National reference documents: National Defence Strategy Implementation Plan, National Army Training Doctrine.

Activities for the project implementation. (1) Construction of one additional compound for simulation training at Bulboaca Training Centre in addition to existing facilities. Bidding process will be carried out by the MOD of Moldova. (2) Equip the Simulation Training Centre with 3 types of simulators: (a) Live (MILES I-HITS type (Multiple Integrated Laser Engagement System

Initial Homestation Instrumentation Training System)); (b) Virtual (VBS type (Virtual Battle Space)); (c) Constructive (JCATS type (Joint Conflict and Tactical Simulation)). Bidding process will be carried out by the MOD of Moldova. (3) Training of the personnel will be organised by the companies providing equipment. Additional training can be provided on bilateral basis by EU member states. (4) Development of the special training programs for simulation, including for international missions training for battalion-size military contingents. (5) Assistance in training of instructors to lead simulative training and exercises. Training can be provided on bilateral basis by EU member states.
Resources needed. Further assessment required.
